sections.heading: Sleeping Temples, Shipwreck Pharmacology, Cuneiform Neurology & Humane Psychiatry

episodes.label: The Grave With Two Calendars — Repton Viking Charnel Deposit, Anglo-Saxon Silver Coin Hoard (873–874 CE) vs. Bone Collagen Radiocarbon & Marine Reservoir Correction
episodes.notes: Archaeometric resolution of the Repton Viking Great Army charnel deposit: why five silver pennies in Grave 529 dated the burial to 873–874 CE while uncalibrated terrestrial bone collagen 14C dates appeared centuries older, and how Jarman et al. (2018) combined delta-13C/delta-15N dietary paleodiet reconstruction with marine reservoir correction (Heaton et al. 2020 Marine20) to reconcile the numismatic and radiocarbon calendars.

episodes.label: The First Anatomists of Speech — 430,000-Yr Ear Bones, Neanderthal Hyoids & Shanidar Care
episodes.notes: Reconstructs Middle Pleistocene speech acoustics from Sima de los Huesos ossicles (2–4 kHz), Kebara 2's hyoid, FOXP2, and Shanidar 1's decades of social survival.

episodes.notes: Synchrotron archaeometry of ancient Egyptian medical/ritual papyri (#39): Christiansen et al.'s (2020 PNAS) sub-micrometer XRF/XRD/FTIR mapping of 12 Tebtunis temple-library fragments showing hematite red-ocher pigment surrounded by sub-visible lead-phosphate/sulfate coffee-ring margins and lead palmitate, copper-bearing soot in Pathyris/Tebtunis black inks (2017), and Sibilia et al.'s (2021) Este Roman bronze inkwell distinguishing carbon-gum ink from container-corrosion cerussite (84% of Pb) and malachite.

sections.heading: Paleosurgery, Ancient Pharmacology & Bedside Clinical Audits

episodes.label: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
episodes.notes: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

episodes.label: The Toe That Had to Walk — Ancient Egyptian Wooden & Cartonnage Prosthetic Great Toes, TT95A Bioarchaeology & Gait Lab Biomechanics
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and biomechanical evaluation of the Cairo wooden toe (JE 100016a from TT95A) and British Museum Greville Chester cartonnage toe (EA29996): healed first-MTP amputation, refitting wear marks, and Finch et al. (2012) Salford gait-lab kinematics and plantar pressure mat experiments.

episodes.label: The Lens That Never Left the Eye — Ancient Cataract Couching in Celsus & Sushruta, α/γ-Crystallin Optics, Aphakic Refraction & Survey Outcomes
episodes.notes: From Celsus and Sushruta's descriptions of cataract couching to alpha/gamma-crystallin short-range order, zonular lysis, why a displaced lens restores light transmission while leaving the eye ~+10 D aphakic, and the 249-eye Nigerian survey separating presenting vs. pinhole-corrected visual acuity.

episodes.label: The Leaf That Came Out Whole — Chimpanzee Rough-Leaf Swallowing, Vernonia Pith, Rakus Wound Care & Neolithic Durrington Coprolites
episodes.notes: Comparative evidence ledger across animal self-medication and paleoparasitology: physical Oesophagostomum worm expulsion via folded Aspilia leaves at Mahale, bitter Vernonia amygdalina sesquiterpene lactones, orangutan Fibraurea wound application, and fecal sterol/aDNA authentication of Neolithic Durrington Walls coprolites.

episodes.label: The Glue, the Chew, and the Wound — Neolithic Syltholm Birch Pitch, Betulin Triterpenes, Ancient Oral Metagenomes & Epidermolysis Bullosa Trials
episodes.notes: From a 5,700-year-old chewed birch bark pitch at Syltholm (Denmark) yielding a complete human genome and oral microbiome to GC-MS betulin/lupeol biomarkers, in vitro agar disk diffusion limits, and the Phase III EASE clinical trial of standardized birch triterpenes in epidermolysis bullosa.

episodes.label: The Tooth That Kept the Tool Marks — Neanderthal Molar Grooves, Villabruna Caries Scraping, Mehrgarh Bow-Drills & Lonche Beeswax
episodes.notes: Scanning electron microscopy, micro-CT, and FTIR spectroscopy of prehistoric worked teeth: Neanderthal interproximal toothpick grooves, Upper Paleolithic Villabruna carious lesion scraping, Neolithic Mehrgarh flint bow-drilled molars, and the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling.

episodes.label: The Spine That Looked Too Dense — Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) Projection Geometry, Aortic Calcification & Contrast Artifacts, Vertebral Exclusions & ISCD Positions
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H037 (DXA Bone Densitometry & Projection Artifacts): how two-energy X-ray attenuation integrates all mineral along the beam path, why an L1 vertebral compression fracture and abdominal aortic calcification produced a high anteroposterior lumbar reading (Gupta et al. 2021), iodinated contrast (+3.8 to -1.5 T-score) and vertebral cement exclusions (+7.7 to -2.6 T-score, White et al. 2025), person-level vs. vertebra-level osteophyte and fracture comparisons in 96 women (Paiva et al. 2002), and the 2023 ISCD Adult Official Positions.

episodes.label: The Tooth They Drilled — Neolithic Mehrgarh Flint Bow-Drills, Villabruna Bitumen & Lonche Beeswax Dental Fillings Under SEM & Synchrotron Micro-CT
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and analytical investigation of prehistoric dentistry: concentric flint drill striations in Neolithic Mehrgarh molars (Coppa et al. 2006), Upper Paleolithic Villabruna and Riparo Fredian cavities, and synchrotron FTIR/radiocarbon verification of the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling (Bernardini et al. 2012).

episodes.label: The Seasons Inside a Tooth — Neanderthal Enamel Retzius Lines, Oxygen Isotopes, Barium Nursing Traces & Lead Bands
episodes.notes: High-resolution laser-ablation and SHRIMP microprobe reading of Neanderthal teeth (Smith et al. 2018): daily enamel cross-striations, seasonal oxygen-18 cycles, barium/calcium nursing transitions, and acute wintertime lead exposure bands.

episodes.label: The Opening That Stayed Open — Copper Age Pontecagnano Cranial Trepanation, Beveled Scraping Remodeling, Femoral Osteomyelitis & Modern CT Margins of Healed Skull Defects
episodes.notes: Osteological and radiological investigation of the 5,000-year-old Copper Age trepanned skull from Pontecagnano, southern Italy (Petrone et al.): broad watch-face outer scraping tapering to a lentil-sized inner aperture, obliterated diploic pores and smooth remodeled margins proving extended survival, severe femoral osteomyelitis in the same individual, and modern surgical CT correlates.

episodes.label: The Medicine We Cannot See — El Sidrón Neanderthal Dental Calculus Pyrolysis-GC/MS & aDNA, Chamomile/Yarrow/Poplar/Penicillium vs. Dental Abscess & Experimental Calculus Entrapment
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and experimental critique of prehistoric non-nutritive plant ingestion: El Sidrón Neanderthal dental calculus pyrolysis-GC/MS and shotgun metagenomics alongside a mandibular dental abscess and Enterocytozoon bieneusi infection (Hardy et al. 2012; Weyrich et al. 2017), experimental herbal mouth-rinse calculus entrapment models, and the evidentiary boundary between dietary/craft/environmental exposure and intentional self-medication.

episodes.label: What the Ice Kept in the Skin — Ötzi the Iceman's 61 Soot Tattoos, Multispectral Reflectance, Pazyryk Mummies & Therapeutic vs. Symbolic Puncturing
episodes.notes: Non-invasive multispectral photographic mapping and histological analysis of preserved ancient skin tattoos in glacial and permafrost mummies (Samadelli et al. 2015 on Ötzi's 61 tattoos across 19 anatomical groups), Raman carbon-soot chemistry, and testing the joint-degeneration acupuncture hypothesis.

episodes.label: The Foot That Healed — 31,000-Year-Old Borneo Distal Lower-Leg Amputation, Cortical Remodeling & Pleistocene Surgical Care
episodes.notes: Osteoarchaeological and paleopathological analysis of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo burial in Borneo (Maloney et al. 2022): healed distal tibia and fibula amputation with 6–9 years of post-operative survival and absence of osteomyelitis.

episodes.label: The Last Meal in the Bog — Tollund Man's Gut Contents, Barley-Flax-Weed Gruel, Whipworm Eggs & Forensic Reconstruction
episodes.notes: Multi-proxy forensic re-analysis of Tollund Man's large-intestinal contents (Nielsen et al. 2021): plant macrofossils, pollen, non-pollen palynomorphs, ancient DNA, proteins, lipids, Trichuris trichiura eggs, and why threshing waste was intentionally added.

episodes.notes: Ancient urban hydrology and geoarchaeology at Classic Maya Tikal (#32): Scarborough et al.'s (2012) reservoir excavation framework, Tankersley et al.'s (2020) discovery of imported volcanogenic clinoptilolite/mordenite zeolites and macrocrystalline quartz in Corriental sediments, Lentz et al.'s (2020) cinnabar-derived mercury and Planktothrix cyanobacterial eDNA in central palace reservoirs, and 2021 arboreal sediment eDNA.

sections.heading: Black Death Genetics, Tuberculosis, HIV & Parasitic Granulomas

episodes.label: The Cheese That Kept a History — 3,500-Year-Old Xiaohe Kefir Dairy Proteomics, Ancient Lactobacillus Genomes, Dental Calculus Milk Peptides & Microbial Niche Partitioning
episodes.notes: Biomolecular archaeology and microbial ecology of Bronze Age fermented dairy from the Tarim Basin: LC-MS/MS proteomics of Xiaohe tomb dairy lumps (Yang et al. 2014), dental calculus milk peptides in seven Xiaohe individuals despite lactase non-persistence genotypes (Zhang et al. 2021), ancient DNA capture and phylogeny of 3,500-year-old Lactobacillus kefiranofaciens strains (Liu et al. 2024), and experimental metabolic cross-feeding in modern kefir communities (Blasche et al. 2021).

episodes.label: The Inheritance in Thin Air — 5,100-Year-Old Zongri Genomes, Denisovan EPAS1 Introgression, Hypoxia Enhancer ENH5 Editing & Endothelial Adaptation
episodes.notes: Evolutionary genomics and functional regulatory biology of high-altitude adaptation on the Tibetan Plateau: 89 ancient genomes spanning 5,100 years beginning at Zongri (Wang et al. 2023), Denisovan-like EPAS1 haplotype introgression and selection timing (Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014; Zhang et al. 2021), hypoxia-responsive ENH5 enhancer reporter and deletion experiments (Gray et al. 2022), and iPSC-derived endothelial transcriptomics under hypoxia (Gray et al. 2025).

episodes.label: The Feast in the Ground — Durrington Walls Near Stonehenge (~2500 BCE), Roasted Pig Bones vs. Dairy/Beef Grooved-Ware Lipids, Multi-Isotope Livestock Mobility & Coprolite Parasites
episodes.notes: Multi-proxy archaeological forensics at Durrington Walls (~2500 BCE): resolving the pig-bone vs. cattle/dairy potsherd lipid paradox through culinary segregation (Craig et al. 2015), five-isotope British livestock provenance (Madgwick et al. 2019), and Mitchell's coprolite paleoparasitology showing poorly cooked bovine/canid-shared tapeworm and capillariid infections.

episodes.label: What Pathogen DNA Can Date — Ancient Treponemal Genomes, Radiocarbon Calibration & Molecular Clock Boundaries
episodes.notes: Paleogenomic investigation of pre-Columbian Treponema pallidum and ancient pathogens (Majander et al. 2024; Barquera et al. 2025; 5,500-year-old Sabana de Bogota genome): damage patterns, radiocarbon priors, recombination filtration, and tip-dating limits.

episodes.label: What the Roman Drain Kept — Roman Latrine Archaeoparasitology, Helminth Eggs, Giardia ELISA & Coprolite Bile-Acid GC-MS
episodes.notes: Multi-proxy archaeoparasitological and biomolecular analysis of Roman sewer and latrine sediments: Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, Taenia spp., and Diphyllobothrium latum microscopy, Giardia duodenalis and Entamoeba histolytica antigen ELISA, and fecal sterol/bile-acid GC-MS.

sections.heading: Cross-Listed Bridges: Iron Age Archaeotoxicology, Botanical Drug Origins & Ancient Texts

episodes.label: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

episodes.label: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
episodes.notes: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

episodes.label: Foxglove, Digoxin & the Number That Rose After Rescue — Withering's Dropsy, Na+/K+-ATPase 4RET, DigiFab Immunoassay Interference & Free vs. Total LC-MS/MS
episodes.notes: From William Withering's 1785 dropsy cases to the 4 A porcine Na+/K+-ATPase crystal structure (4RET), UHPLC-MS/MS MRM transitions, and why ovine DigiFab rescue causes total serum digoxin immunoassays to surge twelvefold while free pharmacologically active digoxin plummets.

episodes.label: The Seal and the Crack — Mohenjo-daro Seal DK5175/143, Shang Oracle Bone Ping 0368 & What Ritual Surfaces Preserve
episodes.notes: Comparative material epistemology of ancient religion: what an undeciphered Mohenjo-daro steatite stamp seal (DK5175/143) vs. a dated Late Shang pyro-osteomantic turtle plastron inscription (Ping 0368) can and cannot prove about supernatural agency and ritual rules.

episodes.label: The Scroll That Stayed Rolled — Virtual Unwrapping from En-Gedi's Metal-Bearing Ink (Seales 2016) to Herculaneum Carbon Ink (Parker 2019) & Complete Surface Reading of PHerc. 1667 & Philodemus's On Gods Book 8
episodes.notes: X-ray micro-CT virtual unwrapping and machine-learned carbon-ink detection in carbonized ancient scrolls: Seales et al.'s (2016) reading of Leviticus inside the charred En-Gedi scroll, Parker et al.'s (2019) 3D voxel ink classification on Herculaneum fragment PHerc. Paris 2 Fr. 96, and Angelotti et al.'s (2026 preprint) end-to-end surface reconstruction of PHerc. 1667 and title identification of Philodemus's On Gods Book 8 in PHerc. 139.
